P13.bad: An improvised roof sags, branches shift, or snow accumulates over the sleeping area.
P13.fix: Move clear of the unstable structure. Use a safer above-ground windbreak and dry ground insulation; keep the exit unobstructed and seek help.
P13.limit: Fallen-branch construction has no verified snow-load capacity. This conceptual drawing does not authorize sleeping beneath an untested roof.

P14.bad: Sparks, shifting wind, smoke, or radiant heat reach shelter fabric or dry covering.
P14.fix: Extinguish or relocate the outdoor fire before it threatens the shelter. Prefer wind protection and dry insulation over risky combustion.
P14.limit: There is no universally safe fire-to-shelter distance. Fire restrictions, local wind, fuel, materials, and ground conditions require separate assessment. Never burn fuel inside an enclosure.

P15.bad: Roofed snow begins cracking or settling, the exit drifts shut, or digging causes heavy sweating and exhaustion.
P15.fix: Do not occupy beneath uncertain snow. Move to existing shelter or a safer open windbreak, protect dry layers, and contact rescue services.
P15.limit: Snow depth is not proof of roof strength. Roofed snow-trench construction requires suitable conditions, trained judgment, equipment, and an escape plan; this draft is not a build specification.

P16.bad: The ceiling settles, cracks appear, an exit becomes obstructed, ventilation deteriorates, or someone brings combustion equipment inside.
P16.fix: Leave an unstable or poorly ventilated enclosure when safely possible. Do not operate fuel-burning heaters in snow shelters; choose safer wind protection and signal for help.
P16.limit: Untrained overhead snow excavation is not a no-equipment survival shortcut. The diagram cannot verify snow stability, oxygen supply, or structural capacity.

P17.bad: Excavation walls slough, stone supports shift, water collects, or a pit becomes difficult to exit.
P17.fix: Stop the excavation and move to stable above-ground ground. Use dry insulation and known-safe shelter without a fire or heater in the excavation.
P17.limit: No soil strength, rock stability, roof loads, or drainage are established. A covered pit is not approved as an improvised winter shelter.

P18.bad: Condensation wets bedding, the entry or ventilation is obstructed, or the frame begins to settle.
P18.fix: Exit an unsafe enclosure, restore unobstructed air and egress from a safe position, replace wet insulation, and seek more dependable shelter.
P18.limit: A warmer-feeling shelter is not evidence of safe air, dry bedding, or load capacity. Do not use combustion heat in enclosed improvised shelters.
